summary: The article examines cybersecurity as the under-discussed hurdle to autonomous vehicles (AVs) and the "City of Tomorrow." It walks through a timeline of developments from September 2023 to March 2024, including V2X security protocols, a data privacy framework, AI-driven defense, a supply chain breach, proposed legislation, and a workforce training initiative. It concludes that secure AVs depend on technology, regulation, collaboration and skilled people.
one_line: Overview of cybersecurity challenges and responses for autonomous vehicles, covering threats, V2X encryption, privacy, AI, supply chains, regulation and workforce training.
key_facts: On September 15, 2023, reports said the AV industry is scrambling to keep pace with cyber threats; a team led by Dr. Emily Robertson of the Autonomous Systems Security Group (ASSG) highlighted AV ecosystem vulnerabilities.

Intrusions can compromise everything from an AV's sensory apparatus to the software algorithms making split-second navigation decisions, and hackers could take control of vehicles, access user data, or disrupt AV networks.
On October 10, 2023, Voyager Innovations unveiled new Vehicle-to-Everything (V2X) communication security protocols.
Voyager Innovations' protocols, introduced by Chief Security Architect Jayden O'Connor, encrypt and authenticate messages between AVs and infrastructure to reduce eavesdropping and spoofing risks.

On November 22, 2023, the International Forum for AV Ethics announced a regulatory framework proposed by privacy advocate Laura Hernández, with strict guidelines for data collection, storage, processing and sharing and granular user control over data.
On December 3, 2023, AI specialist Dr. Kenneth Wu presented findings that AI models can foresee cyber-attack patterns and adapt rapidly to counter them.
Reliance on AI opens a new threat frontier: adversarial attacks designed to deceive or mislead AI algorithms.
On January 15, 2024, a disclosure revealed a critical supply chain breach at a leading AV manufacturer, caused by a compromised component from a minor subcontractor.
The AV Cyber Alliance, spearheaded by Zoe Chang and Michael Ivanov, was formed to set stringent security standards and vetting procedures for all entities in AV development and deployment.
Senator Liam Ford introduced the Autonomous Vehicle Cybersecurity Act of 2024 on February 20, 2024, seeking a legal framework without undue burdens on manufacturers.
On March 2, 2024, Dr. Alice Johnson launched the Cyber Auto Education Initiative (CAEI) to build AV-specialized cybersecurity talent and close the skills gap.
